lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: So shaken as we are, so wan with care,

lines.text: No more shall trenching war channel her fields,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Nor bruise her flow’rets with the armed hoofs

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of hostile paces: those opposed eyes,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Which, like the meteors of a troubled heaven,

lines.speaker: KING

lines.speaker: KING

lines.speaker: KING

lines.text: No more shall cut his master. Therefore, friends,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: As far as to the sepulchre of Christ—

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Forthwith a power of English shall we levy,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Whose arms were molded in their mothers’ womb

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To chase these pagans in those holy fields

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Over whose acres walked those blessed feet

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Which fourteen hundred years ago were nailed

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For our advantage on the bitter cross.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But this our purpose now is twelve month old,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And bootless ’tis to tell you we will go;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Therefore we meet not now. Then let me hear

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of you, my gentle cousin Westmoreland,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: What yesternight our Council did decree

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: In forwarding this dear expedience.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: My liege, this haste was hot in question,

lines.text: But yesternight, when all athwart there came

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Whose worst was that the noble Mortimer,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Leading the men of Herefordshire to fight

lines.text: Against the irregular and wild Glendower,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Such beastly shameless transformation,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND

lines.speaker: KING

lines.speaker: KING

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: This, matched with other did, my gracious lord,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: For more uneven and unwelcome news

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Came from the North, and thus it did import:

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: On Holy-rood day the gallant Hotspur there,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Young Harry Percy, and brave Archibald,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: That ever-valiant and approved Scot,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: At Holmedon met, where they did spend

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: A sad and bloody hour;

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: As by discharge of their artillery,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: And shape of likelihood, the news was told;

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: For he that brought them, in the very heat

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: And pride of their contention did take horse,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Uncertain of the issue any way.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Here is a dear and true-industrious friend,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Sir Walter Blunt, new lighted from his horse,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Stained with the variation of each soil

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Betwixt that Holmedon and this seat of ours;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And he hath brought us smooth and welcome news.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The Earl of Douglas is discomfited;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Ten thousand bold Scots, two-and-twenty knights,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Balked in their own blood, did Sir Walter see

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: On Holmedon’s plains; of prisoners Hotspur took

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Mordake, Earl of Fife and eldest son

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To beaten Douglas, and the Earl of Athol,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of Murray, Angus, and Menteith.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And is not this an honourable spoil,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: A gallant prize? Ha, cousin, is it not?

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: In faith, it is a conquest for a prince to boast of.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Yea, there thou mak’st me sad, and mak’st me sin

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: In envy that my Lord Northumberland

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Should be the father to so blest a son,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: A son who is the theme of honour’s tongue,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Amongst a grove the very straightest plant,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Who is sweet Fortune’s minion and her pride;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Whilst I, by looking on the praise of him,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: See riot and dishonour stain the brow

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of my young Harry. O, that it could be proved

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That some night-tripping fairy had exchanged

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: In cradle-clothes our children where they lay,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And called mine Percy, his Plantagenet!

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Then would I have his Harry, and he mine:

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But let him from my thoughts. What think you, coz,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of this young Percy’s pride? The prisoners,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Which he in this adventure hath surprised

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To his own use he keeps, and sends me word

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I shall have none but Mordake, Earl of Fife.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: This is his uncle’s teaching, this is Worcester,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Malevolent to you in all aspects,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Which makes him prune himself, and bristle up

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: The crest of youth against your dignity.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But I have sent for him to answer this;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And for this cause awhile we must neglect

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Our holy purpose to Jerusalem.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Cousin, on Wednesday next our Council we

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Will hold at Windsor, so inform the lords:

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But come yourself with speed to us again,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For more is to be said and to be done

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Than out of anger can be uttered.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: I will, my liege.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. An Apartment of Prince Henry’s.

lines.text: Enter Prince Henry and Sir John Falstaff.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Now, Hal, what time of day is it, lad?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Thou art so fat-witted, with drinking of old sack, and unbuttoning thee

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: after supper, and sleeping upon benches after noon, that thou hast

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: forgotten to demand that truly which thou wouldst truly know. What a

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: devil hast thou to do with the time of the day? Unless hours were cups

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: of sack, and minutes capons, and clocks the tongues of bawds, and dials

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: the signs of leaping-houses, and the blessed sun himself a fair hot

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: wench in flame-coloured taffeta, I see no reason why thou shouldst be

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: so superfluous to demand the time of the day.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Indeed, you come near me now, Hal, for we that take purses go by the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: moon and the seven stars, and not by Phœbus, he, that wand’ring knight

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: so fair. And I prithee, sweet wag, when thou art king, as God save thy

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Grace—Majesty I should say, for grace thou wilt have none—

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What, none?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: No, by my troth, not so much as will serve to be prologue to an egg and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: butter.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Well, how then? Come, roundly, roundly.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Marry then, sweet wag, when thou art king, let not us that are squires

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: of the night’s body be called thieves of the day’s beauty: let us be

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Diana’s foresters, gentlemen of the shade, minions of the moon; and let

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: men say we be men of good government, being governed, as the sea is, by

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: our noble and chaste mistress the moon, under whose countenance we

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: steal.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Thou sayest well, and it holds well too, for the fortune of us that are

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: the moon’s men doth ebb and flow like the sea, being governed, as the

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: sea is, by the moon. As for proof now: a purse of gold most resolutely

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: snatched on Monday night, and most dissolutely spent on Tuesday

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: morning, got with swearing “Lay by” and spent with crying “Bring in”;

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: now in as low an ebb as the foot of the ladder, and by and by in as

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: high a flow as the ridge of the gallows.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: By the Lord, thou say’st true, lad. And is not my hostess of the tavern

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: a most sweet wench?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: As the honey of Hybla, my old lad of the castle. And is not a buff

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: jerkin a most sweet robe of durance?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: How now, how now, mad wag? What, in thy quips and thy quiddities? What

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: a plague have I to do with a buff jerkin?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Why, what a pox have I to do with my hostess of the tavern?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Well, thou hast called her to a reckoning many a time and oft.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Did I ever call for thee to pay thy part?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: No, I’ll give thee thy due, thou hast paid all there.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Yea, and elsewhere, so far as my coin would stretch, and where it would

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: not, I have used my credit.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Yea, and so used it that were it not here apparent that thou art heir

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: apparent—But I prithee sweet wag, shall there be gallows standing in

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: England when thou art king? And resolution thus fubbed as it is with

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the rusty curb of old father Antic the law? Do not thou, when thou art

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: king, hang a thief.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: No, thou shalt.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Shall I? O rare! By the Lord, I’ll be a brave judge.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Thou judgest false already, I mean thou shalt have the hanging of the

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: thieves, and so become a rare hangman.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Well, Hal, well; and in some sort it jumps with my humour, as well as

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: waiting in the court, I can tell you.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: For obtaining of suits?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Yea, for obtaining of suits, whereof the hangman hath no lean wardrobe.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: ’Sblood, I am as melancholy as a gib cat or a lugged bear.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Or an old lion, or a lover’s lute.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Yea, or the drone of a Lincolnshire bagpipe.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What sayest thou to a hare, or the melancholy of Moor-ditch?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Thou hast the most unsavoury similes, and art indeed the most

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: comparative, rascalliest, sweet young prince. But, Hal, I prithee

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: trouble me no more with vanity. I would to God thou and I knew where a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: commodity of good names were to be bought. An old lord of the Council

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: rated me the other day in the street about you, sir, but I marked him

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: not, and yet he talked very wisely, but I regarded him not, and yet he

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: talked wisely, and in the street too.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Thou didst well, for wisdom cries out in the streets and no man regards

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: it.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: O, thou hast damnable iteration, and art indeed able to corrupt a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: saint. Thou hast done much harm upon me, Hal, God forgive thee for it.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Before I knew thee, Hal, I knew nothing, and now am I, if a man should

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: speak truly, little better than one of the wicked. I must give over

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: this life, and I will give it over. By the Lord, an I do not, I am a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: villain. I’ll be damned for never a king’s son in Christendom.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Where shall we take a purse tomorrow, Jack?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Zounds, where thou wilt, lad, I’ll make one. An I do not, call me

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: villain and baffle me.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I see a good amendment of life in thee, from praying to purse-taking.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Why, Hal, ’tis my vocation, Hal, ’tis no sin for a man to labour in his

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: vocation.
Enter Poins.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Poins!—Now shall we know if Gadshill have set a match. O, if men were

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: to be saved by merit, what hole in hell were hot enough for him? This

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: is the most omnipotent villain that ever cried “Stand!” to a true man.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Good morrow, Ned.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Good morrow, sweet Hal.—What says Monsieur Remorse? What says Sir John

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Sack-and-sugar? Jack, how agrees the devil and thee about thy soul,

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: that thou soldest him on Good Friday last for a cup of Madeira and a

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: cold capon’s leg?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Sir John stands to his word, the devil shall have his bargain, for he

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: was never yet a breaker of proverbs. He will give the devil his due.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Then art thou damned for keeping thy word with the devil.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Else he had been damned for cozening the devil.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: But, my lads, my lads, tomorrow morning, by four o’clock early at Gad’s

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Hill, there are pilgrims going to Canterbury with rich offerings, and

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: traders riding to London with fat purses. I have visards for you all;

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: you have horses for yourselves. Gadshill lies tonight in Rochester. I

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: have bespoke supper tomorrow night in Eastcheap. We may do it as secure

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: as sleep. If you will go, I will stuff your purses full of crowns. If

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: you will not, tarry at home and be hanged.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Hear ye, Yedward, if I tarry at home and go not, I’ll hang you for

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: going.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: You will, chops?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Hal, wilt thou make one?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Who, I rob? I a thief? Not I, by my faith.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: There’s neither honesty, manhood, nor good fellowship in thee, nor thou

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: cam’st not of the blood royal, if thou darest not stand for ten

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: shillings.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Well then, once in my days I’ll be a madcap.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Why, that’s well said.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Well, come what will, I’ll tarry at home.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: By the Lord, I’ll be a traitor then, when thou art king.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I care not.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Sir John, I prithee, leave the Prince and me alone. I will lay him down

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: such reasons for this adventure, that he shall go.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Well, God give thee the spirit of persuasion, and him the ears of

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: profiting, that what thou speakest may move, and what he hears may be

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: believed, that the true prince may, for recreation sake, prove a false

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: thief, for the poor abuses of the time want countenance. Farewell, you

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: shall find me in Eastcheap.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Farewell, thou latter spring! Farewell, All-hallown summer!
[_Exit Falstaff._]

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Now, my good sweet honey lord, ride with us tomorrow. I have a jest to

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: execute that I cannot manage alone. Falstaff, Bardolph, Peto, and

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Gadshill shall rob those men that we have already waylaid. Yourself and

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: I will not be there. And when they have the booty, if you and I do not

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: rob them, cut this head off from my shoulders.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: But how shall we part with them in setting forth?

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Why, we will set forth before or after them, and appoint them a place

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: of meeting, wherein it is at our pleasure to fail; and then will they

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: adventure upon the exploit themselves, which they shall have no sooner

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: achieved but we’ll set upon them.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Yea, but ’tis like that they will know us by our horses, by our habits,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: and by every other appointment, to be ourselves.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Tut, our horses they shall not see, I’ll tie them in the wood; our

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: visards we will change after we leave them; and, sirrah, I have cases

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: of buckram for the nonce, to immask our noted outward garments.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Yea, but I doubt they will be too hard for us.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Well, for two of them, I know them to be as true-bred cowards as ever

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: turned back; and for the third, if he fight longer than he sees reason,

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: I’ll forswear arms. The virtue of this jest will be the

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: incomprehensible lies that this same fat rogue will tell us when we

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: meet at supper: how thirty at least he fought with, what wards, what

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: blows, what extremities he endured; and in the reproof of this lives

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: the jest.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Well, I’ll go with thee. Provide us all things necessary and meet me

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: tomorrow night in Eastcheap; there I’ll sup. Farewell.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Farewell, my lord.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I know you all, and will awhile uphold

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: The unyok’d humour of your idleness.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Yet herein will I imitate the sun,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Who doth permit the base contagious clouds

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: To smother up his beauty from the world,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: That, when he please again to be himself,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Being wanted, he may be more wonder’d at,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: By breaking through the foul and ugly mists

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Of vapours that did seem to strangle him.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: If all the year were playing holidays,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: To sport would be as tedious as to work;

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: But, when they seldom come, they wish’d-for come,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And nothing pleaseth but rare accidents.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: So when this loose behaviour I throw off,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And pay the debt I never promised,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: By how much better than my word I am,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: By so much shall I falsify men’s hopes;

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And, like bright metal on a sullen ground,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: My reformation, glitt’ring o’er my fault,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Shall show more goodly and attract more eyes

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Than that which hath no foil to set it off.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I’ll so offend, to make offence a skill,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Redeeming time, when men think least I will.
