lines.text: I’ll steal to Glendower and Lord Mortimer,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Where you and Douglas, and our powers at once,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: As I will fashion it, shall happily meet,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: To bear our fortunes in our own strong arms,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Which now we hold at much uncertainty.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Farewell, good brother; we shall thrive, I trust.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Uncle, adieu. O, let the hours be short,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Till fields and blows and groans applaud our sport!
[_Exeunt._]
Enter a Carrier with a lantern in his hand.

lines.speaker: FIRST CARRIER
lines.text: Heigh-ho! an it be not four by the day, I’ll be hang’d. Charles’ wain

lines.speaker: FIRST CARRIER
lines.text: is over the new chimney, and yet our horse not pack’d.—What, ostler!
[_within._]

lines.speaker: OSTLER
lines.text: Anon, anon.

lines.speaker: FIRST CARRIER
lines.text: I prithee, Tom, beat Cut’s saddle, put a few flocks in the point; poor

lines.speaker: FIRST CARRIER
lines.text: jade is wrung in the withers out of all cess.
Enter another Carrier.

lines.speaker: SECOND CARRIER
lines.text: Peas and beans are as dank here as a dog, and that is the next way to

lines.speaker: SECOND CARRIER
lines.text: give poor jades the bots. This house is turned upside down since Robin

lines.speaker: SECOND CARRIER
lines.text: ostler died.

lines.speaker: FIRST CARRIER
lines.text: Poor fellow never joyed since the price of oats rose, it was the death

lines.speaker: FIRST CARRIER
lines.text: of him.

lines.speaker: SECOND CARRIER
lines.text: I think this be the most villainous house in all London road for fleas.

lines.speaker: SECOND CARRIER
lines.text: I am stung like a tench.

lines.speaker: FIRST CARRIER
lines.text: Like a tench! By the Mass, there is ne’er a king christen could be

lines.speaker: FIRST CARRIER
lines.text: better bit than I have been since the first cock.

lines.speaker: SECOND CARRIER
lines.text: Why, they will allow us ne’er a jordan, and then we leak in your

lines.speaker: SECOND CARRIER
lines.text: chimney, and your chamber-lye breeds fleas like a loach.

lines.speaker: FIRST CARRIER
lines.text: What, ostler! Come away and be hanged, come away.

lines.speaker: SECOND CARRIER
lines.text: I have a gammon of bacon and two razes of ginger, to be delivered as

lines.speaker: SECOND CARRIER
lines.text: far as Charing Cross.

lines.speaker: FIRST CARRIER
lines.text: God’s body! The turkeys in my pannier are quite starved.—What, ostler!

lines.speaker: FIRST CARRIER
lines.text: A plague on thee! Hast thou never an eye in thy head? Canst not hear?

lines.speaker: FIRST CARRIER
lines.text: An ’twere not as good deed as drink to break the pate on thee, I am a

lines.speaker: FIRST CARRIER
lines.text: very villain. Come, and be hanged. Hast no faith in thee?
Enter Gadshill.

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: Good morrow, carriers. What’s o’clock?

lines.speaker: FIRST CARRIER
lines.text: I think it be two o’clock.

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: I prithee, lend me thy lantern, to see my gelding in the stable.

lines.speaker: FIRST CARRIER
lines.text: Nay, by God, soft! I know a trick worth two of that, i’faith.

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: I pray thee, lend me thine.

lines.speaker: SECOND CARRIER
lines.text: Ay, when? Canst tell? “Lend me thy lantern,” quoth he! Marry, I’ll see

lines.speaker: SECOND CARRIER
lines.text: thee hanged first.

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: Sirrah carrier, what time do you mean to come to London?

lines.speaker: SECOND CARRIER
lines.text: Time enough to go to bed with a candle, I warrant thee. Come, neighbour

lines.speaker: SECOND CARRIER
lines.text: Mugs, we’ll call up the gentlemen. They will along with company, for

lines.speaker: SECOND CARRIER
lines.text: they have great charge.
[_Exeunt Carriers._]

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: What, ho! Chamberlain!
Enter Chamberlain.

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: At hand, quoth pick-purse.

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: That’s even as fair as “at hand, quoth the chamberlain,” for thou

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: variest no more from picking of purses than giving direction doth from

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: labouring; thou layest the plot how.

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: Good morrow, Master Gadshill. It holds current that I told you

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: yesternight: there’s a franklin in the Wild of Kent hath brought three

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: hundred marks with him in gold. I heard him tell it to one of his

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: company last night at supper; a kind of auditor, one that hath

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: abundance of charge too, God knows what. They are up already, and call

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: for eggs and butter. They will away presently.

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: Sirrah, if they meet not with Saint Nicholas’ clerks, I’ll give thee

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: this neck.

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: No, I’ll none of it. I pray thee, keep that for the hangman, for I know

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: thou worshippest Saint Nicholas as truly as a man of falsehood may.

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: What talkest thou to me of the hangman? If I hang, I’ll make a fat pair

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: of gallows; for, if I hang, old Sir John hangs with me, and thou

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: knowest he is no starveling. Tut, there are other Troyans that thou

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: dream’st not of, the which for sport sake are content to do the

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: profession some grace, that would, if matters should be looked into,

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: for their own credit sake make all whole. I am joined with no

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: foot-land-rakers, no long-staff sixpenny strikers, none of these mad

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: mustachio purple-hued malt-worms, but with nobility and tranquillity,

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: burgomasters and great oneyers, such as can hold in, such as will

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: strike sooner than speak, and speak sooner than drink, and drink sooner

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: than pray: and yet, zounds, I lie, for they pray continually to their

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: saint the commonwealth, or rather not pray to her, but prey on her, for

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: they ride up and down on her, and make her their boots.

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: What, the commonwealth their boots? Will she hold out water in foul

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: way?

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: She will, she will; justice hath liquored her. We steal as in a castle,

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: cock-sure; we have the receipt of fern-seed, we walk invisible.

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: Nay, by my faith, I think you are more beholding to the night than to

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: fern-seed for your walking invisible.

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: Give me thy hand. Thou shalt have a share in our purchase, as I am a

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: true man.

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: Nay, rather let me have it, as you are a false thief.

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: Go to; _homo_ is a common name to all men. Bid the ostler bring my

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: gelding out of the stable. Farewell, you muddy knave.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Prince Henry and Poins; Bardolph and Peto at some distance.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Come, shelter, shelter! I have removed Falstaff’s horse, and he frets

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: like a gummed velvet.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Stand close.
[_They retire._]
Enter Falstaff.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Poins! Poins, and be hanged! Poins!
[_Coming forward._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Peace, ye fat-kidneyed rascal! What a brawling dost thou keep!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Where’s Poins, Hal?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: He is walked up to the top of the hill. I’ll go seek him.
[_Retires._]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I am accursed to rob in that thief’s company. The rascal hath removed

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: my horse and tied him I know not where. If I travel but four foot by

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the square further afoot, I shall break my wind. Well, I doubt not but

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: to die a fair death for all this, if I ’scape hanging for killing that

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: rogue. I have forsworn his company hourly any time this two-and-twenty

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: years, and yet I am bewitched with the rogue’s company. If the rascal

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: have not given me medicines to make me love him, I’ll be hanged. It

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: could not be else: I have drunk medicines. Poins! Hal! A plague upon

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: you both! Bardolph! Peto! I’ll starve ere I’ll rob a foot further. An

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: ’twere not as good a deed as drink, to turn true man, and to leave

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: these rogues, I am the veriest varlet that ever chewed with a tooth.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Eight yards of uneven ground is threescore and ten miles afoot with me,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: and the stony-hearted villains know it well enough. A plague upon it

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: when thieves cannot be true one to another! [_They whistle._] Whew! A

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: plague upon you all! Give me my horse, you rogues, give me my horse and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: be hanged!
[_Coming forward._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Peace, you fat guts, lie down, lay thine ear close

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: to the ground, and list if thou canst hear the tread of travellers.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Have you any levers to lift me up again, being down? ’Sblood, I’ll not

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: bear my own flesh so far afoot again for all the coin in thy father’s

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: exchequer. What a plague mean ye to colt me thus?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Thou liest, thou art not colted, thou art uncolted.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I prithee, good Prince Hal, help me to my horse, good king’s son.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Out, ye rogue! Shall I be your ostler?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Hang thyself in thine own heir-apparent garters! If I be ta’en, I’ll

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: peach for this. An I have not ballads made on you all, and sung to

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: filthy tunes, let a cup of sack be my poison—when a jest is so forward,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: and afoot too! I hate it.
Enter Gadshill.

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: Stand!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: So I do, against my will.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: O, ’tis our setter. I know his voice.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Comes forward with Bardolph and Peto.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: What news?

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: Case ye, case ye, on with your visards. There’s money of the King’s

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: coming down the hill, ’tis going to the King’s exchequer.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: You lie, ye rogue, ’tis going to the King’s tavern.

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: There’s enough to make us all.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: To be hanged.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Sirs, you four shall front them in the narrow lane. Ned Poins and I

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: will walk lower; if they ’scape from your encounter, then they light on

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: us.

lines.speaker: PETO
lines.text: How many be there of them?

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: Some eight or ten.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Zounds, will they not rob us?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What, a coward, Sir John Paunch?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Indeed, I am not John of Gaunt, your grandfather, but yet no coward,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Hal.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Well, we leave that to the proof.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Sirrah Jack, thy horse stands behind the hedge. When thou need’st him,

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: there thou shalt find him. Farewell, and stand fast.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Now cannot I strike him, if I should be hanged.
[_aside to Poins._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Ned, where are our disguises?
[_aside to Prince Henry._]

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Here, hard by. Stand close.
[_Exeunt Prince and Poins._]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Now, my masters, happy man be his dole, say I. Every man to his

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: business.
Enter the Travellers.

lines.speaker: FIRST TRAVELLER
lines.text: Come, neighbour, the boy shall lead our horses down the hill; we’ll

lines.speaker: FIRST TRAVELLER
lines.text: walk afoot awhile and ease our legs.

lines.speaker: THIEVES
lines.text: Stand!

lines.speaker: SECOND TRAVELLER
lines.text: Jesu bless us!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Strike, down with them, cut the villains’ throats! Ah, whoreson

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: caterpillars, bacon-fed knaves, they hate us youth. Down with them,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: fleece them!

lines.speaker: FIRST TRAVELLER
lines.text: O, we are undone, both we and ours for ever!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Hang ye, gorbellied knaves, are ye undone? No, ye fat chuffs, I would

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: your store were here! On, bacons, on! What, ye knaves! young men must

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: live. You are grandjurors, are ye? We’ll jure ye, faith.
[_Here they rob them and bind them. Exeunt_]
Enter Prince Henry and Poins in buckram suits.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: The thieves have bound the true men. Now could thou and I rob the

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: thieves, and go merrily to London, it would be argument for a week,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: laughter for a month, and a good jest for ever.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Stand close, I hear them coming.
[_They retire._]
Enter the Thieves again.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Come, my masters, let us share, and then to horse before day. An the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Prince and Poins be not two arrant cowards, there’s no equity stirring.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: There’s no more valour in that Poins than in a wild duck.
[_As they are sharing, the Prince and Poins set upon them._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Your money!

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Villains!
[_Falstaff after a blow or two, and the others run away, leaving the booty behind them._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Got with much ease. Now merrily to horse.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: The thieves are all scatter’d, and possess’d with fear

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: So strongly that they dare not meet each other;

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Each takes his fellow for an officer.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Away, good Ned. Falstaff sweats to death,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And lards the lean earth as he walks along.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Were’t not for laughing, I should pity him.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: How the fat rogue roared!
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Warkworth. A Room in the Castle.

lines.text: Enter Hotspur, reading a letter.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: “But, for mine own part, my lord, I could be well contented to be

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: there, in respect of the love I bear your house.” He could be

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: contented; why is he not, then? In respect of the love he bears our

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: house—he shows in this, he loves his own barn better than he loves our

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: house. Let me see some more. “The purpose you undertake is

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: dangerous”—Why, that’s certain. ’Tis dangerous to take a cold, to

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: sleep, to drink; but I tell you, my lord fool, out of this nettle,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: danger, we pluck this flower, safety. “The purpose you undertake is

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: dangerous, the friends you have named uncertain, the time itself

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: unsorted, and your whole plot too light for the counterpoise of so

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: great an opposition.” Say you so, say you so? I say unto you again, you

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: are a shallow, cowardly hind, and you lie. What a lack-brain is this!

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: By the Lord, our plot is a good plot as ever was laid, our friends true

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: and constant: a good plot, good friends, and full of expectation; an

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: excellent plot, very good friends. What a frosty-spirited rogue is

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: this! Why, my Lord of York commends the plot and the general course of

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: the action. Zounds, an I were now by this rascal, I could brain him

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: with his lady’s fan. Is there not my father, my uncle, and myself? Lord

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Edmund Mortimer, my Lord of York, and Owen Glendower? Is there not

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: besides the Douglas? Have I not all their letters to meet me in arms by

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: the ninth of the next month, and are they not some of them set forward

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: already? What a pagan rascal is this, an infidel! Ha! You shall see

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: now, in very sincerity of fear and cold heart, will he to the King, and

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: lay open all our proceedings. O, I could divide myself, and go to

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: buffets, for moving such a dish of skim milk with so honourable an

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: action! Hang him, let him tell the King, we are prepared. I will set

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: forward tonight.—
Enter Lady Percy.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: How now, Kate! I must leave you within these two hours.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: O my good lord, why are you thus alone?

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: For what offence have I this fortnight been

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: A banish’d woman from my Harry’s bed?

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Tell me, sweet lord, what is’t that takes from thee

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Thy stomach, pleasure, and thy golden sleep?

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Why dost thou bend thine eyes upon the earth,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: And start so often when thou sit’st alone?

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Why hast thou lost the fresh blood in thy cheeks,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: And given my treasures and my rights of thee

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: To thick-eyed musing and curst melancholy?

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: In thy faint slumbers I by thee have watch’d,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: And heard thee murmur tales of iron wars,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Speak terms of manage to thy bounding steed,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Cry “Courage! To the field!” And thou hast talk’d

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Of sallies and retires, of trenches, tents,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Of palisadoes, frontiers, parapets,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Of basilisks, of cannon, culverin,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Of prisoners’ ransom, and of soldiers slain,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: And all the currents of a heady fight.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Thy spirit within thee hath been so at war,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: And thus hath so bestirr’d thee in thy sleep,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: That beads of sweat have stood upon thy brow

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Like bubbles in a late-disturbed stream,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: And in thy face strange motions have appear’d,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Such as we see when men restrain their breath

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: On some great sudden hest. O, what portents are these?

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Some heavy business hath my lord in hand,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: And I must know it, else he loves me not.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: What, ho!
Enter a Servant.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Is Gilliams with the packet gone?

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: He is, my lord, an hour ago.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Hath Butler brought those horses from the sheriff?

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: One horse, my lord, he brought even now.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: What horse? A roan, a crop-ear, is it not?

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: It is, my lord.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: That roan shall be my throne.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Well, I will back him straight. O Esperance!

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Bid Butler lead him forth into the park.
[_Exit Servant._]

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: But hear you, my lord.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: What say’st thou, my lady?

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: What is it carries you away?

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Why, my horse, my love, my horse.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Out, you mad-headed ape!

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: A weasel hath not such a deal of spleen

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: As you are toss’d with. In faith,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: I’ll know your business, Harry, that I will.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: I fear my brother Mortimer doth stir

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: About his title, and hath sent for you

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: To line his enterprise. But if you go—

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: So far afoot, I shall be weary, love.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Come, come, you paraquito, answer me

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Directly unto this question that I ask.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: In faith, I’ll break thy little finger, Harry,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: If thou wilt not tell me all things true.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Away,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Away, you trifler! Love, I love thee not,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: I care not for thee, Kate. This is no world

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: To play with mammets and to tilt with lips.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: We must have bloody noses and crack’d crowns,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And pass them current too.—Gods me, my horse!—

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: What say’st thou, Kate? What wouldst thou have with me?

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Do you not love me? Do you not indeed?

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Well, do not, then, for since you love me not,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: I will not love myself. Do you not love me?

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Nay, tell me if you speak in jest or no.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Come, wilt thou see me ride?

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And when I am a-horseback I will swear

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: I love thee infinitely. But hark you, Kate,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: I must not have you henceforth question me

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Whither I go, nor reason whereabout.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Whither I must, I must; and, to conclude,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: This evening must I leave you, gentle Kate.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: I know you wise, but yet no farther wise

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Than Harry Percy’s wife; constant you are,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: But yet a woman; and for secrecy,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: No lady closer, for I well believe

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Thou wilt not utter what thou dost not know;

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And so far will I trust thee, gentle Kate.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: How? So far?

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Not an inch further. But hark you, Kate,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Whither I go, thither shall you go too.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Today will I set forth, tomorrow you.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Will this content you, Kate?

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: It must, of force.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Eastcheap. A Room in the Boar’s Head Tavern.

lines.text: Enter Prince Henry.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Ned, prithee, come out of that fat room, and lend me thy hand to laugh

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: a little.
Enter Poins.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Where hast been, Hal?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: With three or four loggerheads amongst three or fourscore hogsheads. I

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: have sounded the very base-string of humility. Sirrah, I am sworn

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: brother to a leash of drawers, and can call them all by their Christian

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: names, as Tom, Dick, and Francis. They take it already upon their

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: salvation, that though I be but Prince of Wales, yet I am the king of

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: courtesy, and tell me flatly I am no proud Jack, like Falstaff, but a

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Corinthian, a lad of mettle, a good boy,—by the Lord, so they call

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: me—and when I am King of England, I shall command all the good lads in

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Eastcheap. They call drinking deep, “dyeing scarlet,” and when you

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: breathe in your watering, they cry “Hem!” and bid you “Play it off!” To

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: conclude, I am so good a proficient in one quarter of an hour, that I

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: can drink with any tinker in his own language during my life. I tell

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: thee, Ned, thou hast lost much honour that thou wert not with me in

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: this action; but, sweet Ned—to sweeten which name of Ned, I give thee

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: this pennyworth of sugar, clapped even now into my hand by an

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: underskinker, one that never spake other English in his life than

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: “Eight shillings and sixpence,” and “You are welcome,” with this shrill

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: addition, “Anon, anon, sir! Score a pint of bastard in the Half-moon,”

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: or so. But, Ned, to drive away the time till Falstaff come, I prithee,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: do thou stand in some by-room, while I question my puny drawer to what

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: end he gave me the sugar, and do thou never leave calling “Francis,”

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: that his tale to me may be nothing but “Anon.” Step aside, and I’ll

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: show thee a precedent.
[_Exit Poins._]
[_Within_]

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Francis!

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Thou art perfect.
[_Within_]

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Francis!
Enter Francis.

lines.speaker: FRANCIS
lines.text: Anon, anon, sir.—Look down into the Pomegarnet, Ralph.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Come hither, Francis.

lines.speaker: FRANCIS
lines.text: My lord?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: How long hast thou to serve, Francis?

lines.speaker: FRANCIS
lines.text: Forsooth, five years, and as much as to—
[_within._]

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Francis!

lines.speaker: FRANCIS
lines.text: Anon, anon, sir.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Five year! By’r Lady, a long lease for the clinking of pewter! But,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Francis, darest thou be so valiant as to play the coward with thy

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: indenture, and show it a fair pair of heels, and run from it?

lines.speaker: FRANCIS
lines.text: O Lord, sir, I’ll be sworn upon all the books in England, I could find

lines.speaker: FRANCIS
lines.text: in my heart—
[_within._]

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Francis!

lines.speaker: FRANCIS
lines.text: Anon, sir.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: How old art thou, Francis?

lines.speaker: FRANCIS
lines.text: Let me see, about Michaelmas next I shall be—
[_within._]

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Francis!

lines.speaker: FRANCIS
lines.text: Anon, sir.—Pray, stay a little, my lord.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Nay, but hark you, Francis, for the sugar thou gavest me, ’twas a

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: pennyworth, was’t not?

lines.speaker: FRANCIS
lines.text: O Lord, I would it had been two!

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I will give thee for it a thousand pound. Ask me when thou wilt, and

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: thou shalt have it.
[_within._]

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Francis!

lines.speaker: FRANCIS
lines.text: Anon, anon.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Anon, Francis? No, Francis, but tomorrow, Francis; or, Francis, a

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Thursday; or indeed, Francis, when thou wilt. But, Francis,—

lines.speaker: FRANCIS
lines.text: My lord?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Wilt thou rob this leathern-jerkin, crystal-button, not-pated,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: agate-ring, puke-stocking, caddis-garter, smooth-tongue, Spanish-pouch—

lines.speaker: FRANCIS
lines.text: O Lord, sir, who do you mean?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Why, then, your brown bastard is your only drink, for look you,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Francis, your white canvas doublet will sully. In Barbary, sir, it

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: cannot come to so much.

lines.speaker: FRANCIS
lines.text: What, sir?
[_within._]

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Francis!

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Away, you rogue! Dost thou not hear them call?
[_Here they both call him; the Drawer stands amazed, not knowing which way to go._]
Enter Vintner.

lines.speaker: VINTNER
lines.text: What, stand’st thou still, and hear’st such a calling? Look to the

lines.speaker: VINTNER
lines.text: guests within.
[_Exit Francis._]

lines.speaker: VINTNER
lines.text: My lord, old Sir John with half-a-dozen more are at the door. Shall I

lines.speaker: VINTNER
lines.text: let them in?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Let them alone awhile, and then open the door.
[_Exit Vintner._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Poins!
Enter Poins.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Anon, anon, sir.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Sirrah, Falstaff and the rest of the thieves are at the door; shall we

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: be merry?

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: As merry as crickets, my lad. But hark ye, what cunning match have you

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: made with this jest of the drawer? Come, what’s the issue?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I am now of all humours that have showed themselves humours since the

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: old days of goodman Adam to the pupil age of this present twelve

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: o’clock at midnight.
Enter Francis.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What’s o’clock, Francis?

lines.speaker: FRANCIS
lines.text: Anon, anon, sir.
[_Exit Francis._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: That ever this fellow should have fewer words than a parrot, and yet

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: the son of a woman! His industry is upstairs and downstairs; his

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: eloquence the parcel of a reckoning. I am not yet of Percy’s mind, the

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Hotspur of the north, he that kills me some six or seven dozen of Scots

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: at a breakfast, washes his hands, and says to his wife, “Fie upon this

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: quiet life! I want work.” “O my sweet Harry,” says she, “how many hast

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: thou killed today?” “Give my roan horse a drench,” says he; and

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: answers, “Some fourteen,” an hour after; “a trifle, a trifle.” I

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: prithee, call in Falstaff. I’ll play Percy, and that damned brawn shall

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: play Dame Mortimer his wife. _Rivo!_ says the drunkard. Call in Ribs,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: call in Tallow.
Enter Falstaff, Gadshill, Bardolph and Peto; followed by Francis with wine.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Welcome, Jack. Where hast thou been?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: A plague of all cowards, I say, and a vengeance too! Marry, and amen!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Give me a cup of sack, boy. Ere I lead this life long, I’ll sew

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: nether-stocks, and mend them and foot them too. A plague of all

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: cowards! Give me a cup of sack, rogue. Is there no virtue extant?
[_Drinks._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Didst thou never see Titan kiss a dish of butter (pitiful-hearted

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Titan!), that melted at the sweet tale of the sun’s? If thou didst,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: then behold that compound.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: You rogue, here’s lime in this sack too: there is nothing but roguery

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: to be found in villainous man, yet a coward is worse than a cup of sack

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: with lime in it. A villanous coward! Go thy ways, old Jack. Die when

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: thou wilt, if manhood, good manhood, be not forgot upon the face of the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Earth, then am I a shotten herring. There lives not three good men

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: unhanged in England, and one of them is fat, and grows old, God help

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the while, a bad world, I say. I would I were a weaver; I could sing

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: psalms or anything. A plague of all cowards, I say still.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: How now, wool-sack, what mutter you?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: A king’s son! If I do not beat thee out of thy kingdom with a dagger of

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: lath, and drive all thy subjects afore thee like a flock of wild-geese,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I’ll never wear hair on my face more. You, Prince of Wales!

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Why, you whoreson round man, what’s the matter?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Are not you a coward? Answer me to that—and Poins there?

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Zounds, ye fat paunch, an ye call me coward, by the Lord, I’ll stab

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: thee.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I call thee coward? I’ll see thee damned ere I call thee coward, but I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: would give a thousand pound I could run as fast as thou canst. You are

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: straight enough in the shoulders, you care not who sees your back. Call

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: you that backing of your friends? A plague upon such backing! Give me

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: them that will face me.—Give me a cup of sack. I am a rogue if I drunk

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: today.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: O villain! Thy lips are scarce wiped since thou drunk’st last.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: All is one for that. A plague of all cowards, still say I.
[_Drinks._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What’s the matter?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What’s the matter? There be four of us here have ta’en a thousand pound

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: this day morning.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Where is it, Jack, where is it?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Where is it? Taken from us it is: a hundred upon poor four of us.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What, a hundred, man?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I am a rogue if I were not at half-sword with a dozen of them two hours

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: together. I have ’scaped by miracle. I am eight times thrust through

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the doublet, four through the hose, my buckler cut through and through,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: my sword hacked like a handsaw. _Ecce signum!_ I never dealt better

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: since I was a man: all would not do. A plague of all cowards! Let them

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: speak. If they speak more or less than truth, they are villains, and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the sons of darkness.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Speak, sirs, how was it?

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: We four set upon some dozen.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Sixteen at least, my lord.

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: And bound them.

lines.speaker: PETO
lines.text: No, no, they were not bound.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: You rogue, they were bound, every man of them, or I am a Jew else, an

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Ebrew Jew.

lines.speaker: GADSHILL
lines.text: As we were sharing, some six or seven fresh men set upon us.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: And unbound the rest, and then come in the other.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What, fought you with them all?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: All? I know not what you call all, but if I fought not with fifty of

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: them I am a bunch of radish. If there were not two or three and fifty

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: upon poor old Jack, then am I no two-legged creature.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Pray God you have not murdered some of them.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Nay, that’s past praying for. I have peppered two of them. Two I am

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: sure I have paid, two rogues in buckram suits. I tell thee what, Hal,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: if I tell thee a lie, spit in my face, call me horse. Thou knowest my

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: old ward. Here I lay, and thus I bore my point. Four rogues in buckram

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: let drive at me.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What, four? Thou saidst but two even now.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Four, Hal, I told thee four.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Ay, ay, he said four.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: These four came all afront, and mainly thrust at me. I made me no more

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: ado, but took all their seven points in my target, thus.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Seven? Why, there were but four even now.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: In buckram?

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Ay, four, in buckram suits.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Seven, by these hilts, or I am a villain else.
[_aside to Poins._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Prithee let him alone, we shall have more anon.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Dost thou hear me, Hal?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Ay, and mark thee too, Jack.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Do so, for it is worth the listening to. These nine in buckram that I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: told thee of—

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: So, two more already.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Their points being broken—

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Down fell their hose.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Began to give me ground; but I followed me close, came in foot and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: hand, and with a thought seven of the eleven I paid.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: O monstrous! Eleven buckram men grown out of two!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: But as the devil would have it, three misbegotten knaves in Kendal

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: green came at my back and let drive at me, for it was so dark, Hal,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: that thou couldst not see thy hand.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: These lies are like the father that begets them, gross as a mountain,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: open, palpable. Why, thou clay-brained guts, thou knotty-pated fool,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: thou whoreson, obscene greasy tallow-catch—

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What, art thou mad? Art thou mad? Is not the truth the truth?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Why, how couldst thou know these men in Kendal green, when it was so

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: dark thou couldst not see thy hand? Come, tell us your reason. What

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: sayest thou to this?

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Come, your reason, Jack, your reason.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What, upon compulsion? Zounds, an I were at the strappado, or all the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: racks in the world, I would not tell you on compulsion. Give you a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: reason on compulsion! If reasons were as plentiful as blackberries, I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: would give no man a reason upon compulsion, I.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I’ll be no longer guilty of this sin. This sanguine coward, this

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: bed-presser, this horse-back-breaker, this huge hill of flesh—

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: ’Sblood, you starveling, you eel-skin, you dried neat’s-tongue, you

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: bull’s pizzle, you stock-fish—O, for breath to utter what is like thee!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: You tailor’s-yard, you sheath, you bow-case, you vile standing tuck—

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Well, breathe awhile, and then to it again, and when thou hast tired

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: thyself in base comparisons, hear me speak but this.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Mark, Jack.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: We two saw you four set on four, and bound them and were masters of

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: their wealth. Mark now how a plain tale shall put you down. Then did we

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: two set on you four, and, with a word, outfaced you from your prize,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: and have it, yea, and can show it you here in the house. And, Falstaff,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: you carried your guts away as nimbly, with as quick dexterity, and

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: roared for mercy, and still ran and roared, as ever I heard bull-calf.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What a slave art thou to hack thy sword as thou hast done, and then say

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: it was in fight! What trick, what device, what starting-hole canst thou

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: now find out to hide thee from this open and apparent shame?

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Come, let’s hear, Jack, what trick hast thou now?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: By the Lord, I knew ye as well as he that made ye. Why, hear you, my

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: masters, was it for me to kill the heir-apparent? Should I turn upon

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the true prince? Why, thou knowest I am as valiant as Hercules: but

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: beware instinct. The lion will not touch the true prince. Instinct is a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: great matter. I was now a coward on instinct. I shall think the better

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: of myself, and thee, during my life—I for a valiant lion, and thou for

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: a true prince. But, by the Lord, lads, I am glad you have the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: money.—Hostess, clap to the doors. Watch tonight, pray tomorrow.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Gallants, lads, boys, hearts of gold, all the titles of good fellowship

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: come to you! What, shall we be merry? Shall we have a play extempore?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Content; and the argument shall be thy running away.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Ah, no more of that, Hal, an thou lovest me!
Enter the Hostess.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: O Jesu, my lord the Prince—

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: How now, my lady the hostess! What say’st thou to me?

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Marry, my lord, there is a nobleman of the court at door would speak

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: with you: he says he comes from your father.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Give him as much as will make him a royal man, and send him back again

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: to my mother.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What manner of man is he?

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: An old man.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What doth gravity out of his bed at midnight? Shall I give him his

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: answer?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Prithee do, Jack.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Faith, and I’ll send him packing.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Now, sirs: by’r Lady, you fought fair, so did you, Peto. So did you,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Bardolph. You are lions, too, you ran away upon instinct, you will not

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: touch the true prince, no, fie!

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Faith, I ran when I saw others run.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Faith, tell me now in earnest, how came Falstaff’s sword so hacked?

lines.speaker: PETO
lines.text: Why, he hacked it with his dagger, and said he would swear truth out of

lines.speaker: PETO
lines.text: England but he would make you believe it was done in fight, and

lines.speaker: PETO
lines.text: persuaded us to do the like.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Yea, and to tickle our noses with spear-grass to make them bleed, and

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: then to beslubber our garments with it, and swear it was the blood of

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: true men. I did that I did not this seven year before: I blushed to

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: hear his monstrous devices.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: O villain, thou stolest a cup of sack eighteen years ago, and wert

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: taken with the manner, and ever since thou hast blushed extempore. Thou

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: hadst fire and sword on thy side, and yet thou ran’st away. What

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: instinct hadst thou for it?

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: My lord, do you see these meteors? Do you behold these exhalations?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I do.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: What think you they portend?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Hot livers and cold purses.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Choler, my lord, if rightly taken.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: No, if rightly taken, halter.
Enter Falstaff.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Here comes lean Jack, here comes bare-bone. How now, my sweet creature

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: of bombast? How long is’t ago, Jack, since thou sawest thine own knee?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: My own knee? When I was about thy years, Hal, I was not an eagle’s

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: talon in the waist. I could have crept into any alderman’s thumb-ring:

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: a plague of sighing and grief! It blows a man up like a bladder.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: There’s villanous news abroad: here was Sir John Bracy from your

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: father; you must to the court in the morning. That same mad fellow of

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the north, Percy, and he of Wales that gave Amamon the bastinado, and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: made Lucifer cuckold, and swore the devil his true liegeman upon the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: cross of a Welsh hook—what a plague call you him?

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: O, Glendower.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Owen, Owen, the same; and his son-in-law Mortimer, and old

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Northumberland, and that sprightly Scot of Scots, Douglas, that runs

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: a-horseback up a hill perpendicular—

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: He that rides at high speed, and with his pistol kills a sparrow

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: flying.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: You have hit it.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: So did he never the sparrow.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Well, that rascal hath good metal in him, he will not run.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Why, what a rascal art thou then, to praise him so for running!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: A-horseback, ye cuckoo, but afoot he will not budge a foot.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Yes, Jack, upon instinct.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I grant ye, upon instinct. Well, he is there too, and one Mordake, and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: a thousand blue-caps more. Worcester is stolen away tonight; thy

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: father’s beard is turned white with the news. You may buy land now as

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: cheap as stinking mackerel.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Why then, it is like if there come a hot June, and this civil buffeting

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: hold, we shall buy maidenheads as they buy hobnails, by the hundreds.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: By the mass, lad, thou sayest true. It is like we shall have good

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: trading that way. But tell me, Hal, art not thou horrible afeard? Thou

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: being heir-apparent, could the world pick thee out three such enemies

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: again as that fiend Douglas, that spirit Percy, and that devil

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Glendower? Art thou not horribly afraid? Doth not thy blood thrill at

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: it?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Not a whit, i’faith. I lack some of thy instinct.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Well, thou wilt be horribly chid tomorrow when thou comest to thy

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: father. If thou love me practise an answer.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Do thou stand for my father and examine me upon the particulars of my

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: life.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Shall I? Content! This chair shall be my state, this dagger my sceptre,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: and this cushion my crown.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Thy state is taken for a joint-stool, thy golden sceptre for a leaden

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: dagger, and thy precious rich crown for a pitiful bald crown.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Well, an the fire of grace be not quite out of thee, now shalt thou be

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: moved. Give me a cup of sack to make my eyes look red, that it may be

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: thought I have wept, for I must speak in passion, and I will do it in

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: King Cambyses’ vein.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Well, here is my leg.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: And here is my speech. Stand aside, nobility.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: O Jesu, this is excellent sport, i faith!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Weep not, sweet Queen, for trickling tears are vain.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: O, the Father, how he holds his countenance!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: For God’s sake, lords, convey my tristful Queen,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: For tears do stop the floodgates of her eyes.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: O Jesu, he doth it as like one of these harlotry players as ever I see!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Peace, good pint-pot; peace, good tickle-brain.—Harry, I do not only

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: marvel where thou spendest thy time, but also how thou art accompanied.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: For though the camomile, the more it is trodden on, the faster it

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: grows, yet youth, the more it is wasted, the sooner it wears. That thou

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: art my son I have partly thy mother’s word, partly my own opinion, but

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: chiefly a villainous trick of thine eye, and a foolish hanging of thy

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: nether lip, that doth warrant me. If then thou be son to me, here lies

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the point: why, being son to me, art thou so pointed at? Shall the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: blessed sun of heaven prove a micher, and eat blackberries? A question

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: not to be asked. Shall the son of England prove a thief, and take

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: purses? A question to be asked. There is a thing, Harry, which thou

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: hast often heard of, and it is known to many in our land by the name of

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: pitch. This pitch, as ancient writers do report, doth defile; so doth

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the company thou keepest. For, Harry, now I do not speak to thee in

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: drink, but in tears; not in pleasure, but in passion; not in words

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: only, but in woes also. And yet there is a virtuous man whom I have

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: often noted in thy company, but I know not his name.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What manner of man, an it like your Majesty?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: A goodly portly man, i’faith, and a corpulent; of a cheerful look, a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: pleasing eye, and a most noble carriage; and, as I think, his age some

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: fifty, or, by’r Lady, inclining to threescore; and now I remember me,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: his name is Falstaff. If that man should be lewdly given, he deceiveth

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: me; for, Harry, I see virtue in his looks. If then the tree may be

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: known by the fruit, as the fruit by the tree, then peremptorily I speak

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: it, there is virtue in that Falstaff; him keep with, the rest banish.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: And tell me now, thou naughty varlet, tell me where hast thou been this

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: month?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Dost thou speak like a king? Do thou stand for me, and I’ll play my

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: father.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Depose me? If thou dost it half so gravely, so majestically, both in

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: word and matter, hang me up by the heels for a rabbit-sucker or a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: poulter’s hare.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Well, here I am set.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: And here I stand. Judge, my masters.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Now, Harry, whence come you?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: My noble lord, from Eastcheap.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: The complaints I hear of thee are grievous.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: ’Sblood, my lord, they are false.—Nay, I’ll tickle ye for a young

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: prince, i’faith.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Swearest thou, ungracious boy? Henceforth ne’er look on me. Thou art

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: violently carried away from grace. There is a devil haunts thee in the

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: likeness of an old fat man. A tun of man is thy companion. Why dost

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: thou converse with that trunk of humours, that bolting-hutch of

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: beastliness, that swollen parcel of dropsies, that huge bombard of

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: sack, that stuffed cloak-bag of guts, that roasted Manningtree ox with

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: the pudding in his belly, that reverend Vice, that grey iniquity, that

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: father ruffian, that vanity in years? Wherein is he good, but to taste

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: sack and drink it? Wherein neat and cleanly, but to carve a capon and

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: eat it? Wherein cunning, but in craft? Wherein crafty, but in villany?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Wherein villainous, but in all things? Wherein worthy, but in nothing?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I would your Grace would take me with you. Whom means your Grace?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: That villainous abominable misleader of youth, Falstaff, that old

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: white-bearded Satan.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: My lord, the man I know.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I know thou dost.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: But to say I know more harm in him than in myself were to say more than

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I know. That he is old, the more the pity, his white hairs do witness

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: it. But that he is, saving your reverence, a whoremaster, that I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: utterly deny. If sack and sugar be a fault, God help the wicked! If to

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: be old and merry be a sin, then many an old host that I know is damned.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: If to be fat be to be hated, then Pharaoh’s lean kine are to be loved.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: No, my good lord, banish Peto, banish Bardolph, banish Poins, but for

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: sweet Jack Falstaff, kind Jack Falstaff, true Jack Falstaff, valiant

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Jack Falstaff, and therefore more valiant, being as he is old Jack

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Falstaff, banish not him thy Harry’s company, banish not him thy

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Harry’s company. Banish plump Jack, and banish all the world.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I do, I will.
[_A knocking heard._]
[_Exeunt Hostess, Francis and Bardolph._]
Enter Bardolph, running.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: O, my lord, my lord, the sheriff with a most monstrous watch is at the

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: door.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Out, ye rogue! Play out the play. I have much to say in the behalf of

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: that Falstaff.
Enter the Hostess, hastily.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: O Jesu, my lord, my lord—

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Heigh, heigh, the devil rides upon a fiddlestick. What’s the matter?

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: The sheriff and all the watch are at the door. They are come to search

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: the house. Shall I let them in?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Dost thou hear, Hal? Never call a true piece of gold a counterfeit:

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: thou art essentially made without seeming so.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And thou a natural coward without instinct.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I deny your major. If you will deny the sheriff, so; if not, let him

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: enter. If I become not a cart as well as another man, a plague on my

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: bringing up! I hope I shall as soon be strangled with a halter as

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: another.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Go hide thee behind the arras. The rest walk up above. Now, my masters,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: for a true face and good conscience.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Both which I have had, but their date is out, and therefore I’ll hide

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: me.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Call in the sheriff.
[_Exeunt all but the Prince and Peto._]
Enter Sheriff and the Carrier.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Now, master sheriff, what is your will with me?

lines.speaker: SHERIFF
lines.text: First, pardon me, my lord. A hue and cry

lines.speaker: SHERIFF
lines.text: Hath followed certain men unto this house.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What men?

lines.speaker: SHERIFF
lines.text: One of them is well known, my gracious lord,

lines.speaker: SHERIFF
lines.text: A gross fat man.

lines.speaker: CARRIER
lines.text: As fat as butter.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: The man I do assure you is not here,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: For I myself at this time have employ’d him.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And, sheriff, I will engage my word to thee,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: That I will by tomorrow dinner-time,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Send him to answer thee, or any man,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: For anything he shall be charged withal.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And so let me entreat you leave the house.

lines.speaker: SHERIFF
lines.text: I will, my lord. There are two gentlemen

lines.speaker: SHERIFF
lines.text: Have in this robbery lost three hundred marks.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: It may be so. If he have robb’d these men,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: He shall be answerable; and so, farewell.

lines.speaker: SHERIFF
lines.text: Good night, my noble lord.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I think it is good morrow, is it not?

lines.speaker: SHERIFF
lines.text: Indeed, my lord, I think it be two o’clock.
[_Exit Sheriff with the Carrier._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: This oily rascal is known as well as Paul’s. Go, call him forth.

lines.speaker: PETO
lines.text: Falstaff!—Fast asleep behind the arras, and snorting like a horse.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Hark, how hard he fetches breath. Search his pockets.
[_He searcheth his pocket, and findeth certain papers._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What hast thou found?

lines.speaker: PETO
lines.text: Nothing but papers, my lord.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Let’s see what they be. Read them.
[_reads_]

lines.speaker: PETO
lines.text: Item, a capon, . . . . . . . . . . . 2s. 2d.

lines.speaker: PETO
lines.text: Item, sack, two gallons, . . . 5s. 8d.

lines.speaker: PETO
lines.text: Item, anchovies and sack after supper, 2s. 6d.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: O monstrous! But one halfpennyworth of bread to this intolerable deal

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: of sack! What there is else, keep close. We’ll read it at more

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: advantage. There let him sleep till day. I’ll to the court in the

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: morning. We must all to the wars, and thy place shall be honourable.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I’ll procure this fat rogue a charge of foot, and I know his death will

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: be a march of twelve score. The money shall be paid back again with

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: advantage. Be with me betimes in the morning; and so, good morrow,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Peto.

lines.speaker: PETO
lines.text: Good morrow, good my lord.
[_Exeunt._]

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Why, so it would have done

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR

lines.text: And I say the Earth was not of my mind,

lines.text: Is with a kind of colic pinch’d and vex’d

lines.text: Our grandam Earth, having this distemp’rature,

lines.text: Why, so can I, or so can any man,
