lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: According to our threefold order ta’en?

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: The archdeacon hath divided it

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Into three limits very equally:

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: England, from Trent and Severn hitherto,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: By south and east is to my part assign’d:

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: All westward, Wales beyond the Severn shore,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And all the fertile land within that bound,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: To Owen Glendower: and, dear coz, to you

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: The remnant northward lying off from Trent.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And our indentures tripartite are drawn,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Which being sealed interchangeably,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: A business that this night may execute,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Tomorrow, cousin Percy, you and I,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And my good Lord of Worcester will set forth

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: To meet your father and the Scottish power,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: As is appointed us, at Shrewsbury.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: My father Glendower is not ready yet,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Nor shall we need his help these fourteen days.
[_To Glendower._]

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Within that space you may have drawn together

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Your tenants, friends, and neighbouring gentlemen.

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: A shorter time shall send me to you, lords,

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: And in my conduct shall your ladies come,

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: From whom you now must steal, and take no leave,

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: For there will be a world of water shed

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: Upon the parting of your wives and you.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Methinks my moiety, north from Burton here,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: In quantity equals not one of yours.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: See how this river comes me cranking in,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And cuts me from the best of all my land

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: A huge half-moon, a monstrous cantle out.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: I’ll have the current in this place dammed up,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And here the smug and silver Trent shall run

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: In a new channel, fair and evenly.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: It shall not wind with such a deep indent,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: To rob me of so rich a bottom here.

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: Not wind? It shall, it must. You see it doth.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Yea, but mark how he bears his course, and runs me up

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: With like advantage on the other side,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Gelding the opposed continent as much

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: As on the other side it takes from you.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Yea, but a little charge will trench him here,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: And on this north side win this cape of land,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: And then he runs straight and even.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: I’ll have it so, a little charge will do it.

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: I’ll not have it altered.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Will not you?

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: No, nor you shall not.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Who shall say me nay?

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: Why, that will I.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Let me not understand you, then; speak it in Welsh.

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: I can speak English, lord, as well as you,

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: For I was train’d up in the English Court,

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: Where being but young I framed to the harp

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: Many an English ditty lovely well,

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: And gave the tongue a helpful ornament—

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: A virtue that was never seen in you.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Marry, and I am glad of it with all my heart.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: I had rather be a kitten, and cry “mew”

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Than one of these same metre ballad-mongers;

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: I had rather hear a brazen canstick turn’d,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Or a dry wheel grate on the axletree,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And that would set my teeth nothing on edge,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Nothing so much as mincing poetry.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: ’Tis like the forced gait of a shuffling nag.

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: Come, you shall have Trent turn’d.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: I do not care. I’ll give thrice so much land

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: To any well-deserving friend;

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: But in the way of bargain, mark ye me,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: I’ll cavil on the ninth part of a hair.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Are the indentures drawn? Shall we be gone?

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: The moon shines fair, you may away by night.

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: I’ll haste the writer, and withal

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: Break with your wives of your departure hence.

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: I am afraid my daughter will run mad,

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: So much she doteth on her Mortimer.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Fie, cousin Percy, how you cross my father!

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: I cannot choose. Sometimes he angers me

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: With telling me of the moldwarp and the ant,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Of the dreamer Merlin and his prophecies,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And of a dragon and a finless fish,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: A clip-wing’d griffin and a moulten raven,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: A couching lion and a ramping cat,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And such a deal of skimble-skamble stuff

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: As puts me from my faith. I tell you what—

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: He held me last night at least nine hours

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: In reckoning up the several devils’ names

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: That were his lackeys: I cried “Hum,” and “Well, go to,”

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: But mark’d him not a word. O, he is as tedious

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: As a tired horse, a railing wife,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Worse than a smoky house. I had rather live

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: With cheese and garlic in a windmill, far,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Than feed on cates and have him talk to me

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: In any summer house in Christendom.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: In faith, he is a worthy gentleman,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Exceedingly well read, and profited

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: In strange concealments, valiant as a lion,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And wondrous affable, and as bountiful

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: As mines of India. Shall I tell you, cousin?

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: He holds your temper in a high respect

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And curbs himself even of his natural scope

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: When you come cross his humour, faith, he does.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: I warrant you that man is not alive

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Might so have tempted him as you have done

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Without the taste of danger and reproof:

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: But do not use it oft, let me entreat you.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: In faith, my lord, you are too wilful-blame,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: And since your coming hither have done enough

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: To put him quite besides his patience.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: You must needs learn, lord, to amend this fault.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Though sometimes it show greatness, courage, blood—

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: And that’s the dearest grace it renders you—

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Yet oftentimes it doth present harsh rage,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Defect of manners, want of government,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Pride, haughtiness, opinion, and disdain,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: The least of which haunting a nobleman

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Loseth men’s hearts and leaves behind a stain

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Upon the beauty of all parts besides,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Beguiling them of commendation.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Well, I am school’d. Good manners be your speed!

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Here come our wives, and let us take our leave.
Enter Glendower with Lady Mortimer and Lady Percy.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: This is the deadly spite that angers me,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: My wife can speak no English, I no Welsh.

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: My daughter weeps, she’ll not part with you,

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: She’ll be a soldier too, she’ll to the wars.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Good father, tell her that she and my aunt Percy

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Shall follow in your conduct speedily.
[_Glendower speaks to Lady Mortimer in Welsh, and she answers him in the same._]

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: She is desperate here, a peevish self-willed harlotry,

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: One that no persuasion can do good upon.
[_Lady Mortimer speaks to Mortimer in Welsh._]

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: I understand thy looks, that pretty Welsh

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Which thou pourest down from these swelling heavens

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: I am too perfect in, and but for shame

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: In such a parley should I answer thee.
[_Lady Mortimer speaks to him again in Welsh._]

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: I understand thy kisses, and thou mine,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And that’s a feeling disputation,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: But I will never be a truant, love,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Till I have learnt thy language; for thy tongue

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Makes Welsh as sweet as ditties highly penn’d,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Sung by a fair queen in a summer’s bower,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: With ravishing division, to her lute.

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: Nay, if you melt, then will she run mad.
[_Lady Mortimer speaks to Mortimer again in Welsh._]

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: O, I am ignorance itself in this!

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: She bids you on the wanton rushes lay you down,

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: And rest your gentle head upon her lap,

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: And she will sing the song that pleaseth you,

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: And on your eyelids crown the god of sleep,

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: Charming your blood with pleasing heaviness,

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: Making such difference ’twixt wake and sleep

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: As is the difference betwixt day and night,

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: The hour before the heavenly-harness’d team

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: Begins his golden progress in the east.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: With all my heart I’ll sit and hear her sing,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: By that time will our book, I think, be drawn.

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: Do so, and those musicians that shall play to you

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: Hang in the air a thousand leagues from hence,

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: And straight they shall be here: sit, and attend.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Come, Kate, thou art perfect in lying down.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Come, quick, quick, that I may lay my head in thy lap.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Go, ye giddy goose.
[_The music plays._]

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Now I perceive the devil understands Welsh,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And ’tis no marvel he’s so humorous.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: By’r Lady, he’s a good musician.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Then should you be nothing but musical,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: For you are altogether governed by humours.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Lie still, ye thief, and hear the lady sing in Welsh.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: I had rather hear Lady, my brach, howl in Irish.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Wouldst thou have thy head broken?

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Then be still.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Neither; ’tis a woman’s fault.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Now God help thee!

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: To the Welsh lady’s bed.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: What’s that?

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Peace, she sings.
[_Here the lady sings a Welsh song._]

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Come, Kate, I’ll have your song too.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Not mine, in good sooth.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Not yours, in good sooth! Heart! you swear like a comfit-maker’s wife!

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: “Not you, in good sooth,” and “As true as I live,” and “As God shall

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: mend me,” and “As sure as day”

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And givest such sarcenet surety for thy oaths

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: As if thou never walk’dst further than Finsbury.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Swear me, Kate, like a lady as thou art,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: A good mouth-filling oath, and leave “In sooth,”

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And such protest of pepper-gingerbread,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: To velvet-guards and Sunday citizens.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Come, sing.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: I will not sing.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: ’Tis the next way to turn tailor, or be redbreast-teacher. An the

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: indentures be drawn, I’ll away within these two hours; and so come in

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: when ye will.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: Come, come, Lord Mortimer, you are as slow

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: As hot Lord Percy is on fire to go.

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: By this our book is drawn. We’ll but seal,

lines.speaker: GLENDOWER
lines.text: And then to horse immediately.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: With all my heart.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: London. A Room in the Palace.

lines.text: Enter King Henry, Prince Henry and Lords.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Lords, give us leave; the Prince of Wales and I

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Must have some private conference: but be near at hand,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For we shall presently have need of you.
[_Exeunt Lords._]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I know not whether God will have it so

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For some displeasing service I have done,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That, in His secret doom, out of my blood

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: He’ll breed revengement and a scourge for me;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But thou dost in thy passages of life

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Make me believe that thou art only mark’d

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For the hot vengeance and the rod of heaven

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To punish my mistreadings. Tell me else,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Could such inordinate and low desires,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Such poor, such bare, such lewd, such mean attempts,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Such barren pleasures, rude society,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: As thou art match’d withal, and grafted to,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Accompany the greatness of thy blood,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And hold their level with thy princely heart?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: So please your Majesty, I would I could

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Quit all offences with as clear excuse

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: As well as I am doubtless I can purge

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Myself of many I am charged withal.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Yet such extenuation let me beg

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: As, in reproof of many tales devised,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: By smiling pickthanks and base newsmongers,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Which oft the ear of greatness needs must hear,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I may for some things true, wherein my youth

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Hath faulty wander’d and irregular,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Find pardon on my true submission.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: God pardon thee! Yet let me wonder, Harry,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: At thy affections, which do hold a wing

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Quite from the flight of all thy ancestors.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thy place in Council thou hast rudely lost,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Which by thy younger brother is supplied,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And art almost an alien to the hearts

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of all the court and princes of my blood.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The hope and expectation of thy time

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Is ruin’d, and the soul of every man

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Prophetically do forethink thy fall.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Had I so lavish of my presence been,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: So common-hackney’d in the eyes of men,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: So stale and cheap to vulgar company,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Opinion, that did help me to the crown,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Had still kept loyal to possession,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And left me in reputeless banishment,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: A fellow of no mark nor likelihood.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: By being seldom seen, I could not stir

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But like a comet I was wonder’d at,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That men would tell their children, “This is he.”

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Others would say, “Where, which is Bolingbroke?”

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And then I stole all courtesy from heaven,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And dress’d myself in such humility

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That I did pluck allegiance from men’s hearts,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Loud shouts and salutations from their mouths,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Even in the presence of the crowned King.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thus did I keep my person fresh and new,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: My presence, like a robe pontifical,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Ne’er seen but wonder’d at, and so my state,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Seldom but sumptuous, showed like a feast,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And won by rareness such solemnity.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The skipping King, he ambled up and down

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: With shallow jesters and rash bavin wits,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Soon kindled and soon burnt; carded his state,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Mingled his royalty, with cap’ring fools,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Had his great name profaned with their scorns,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And gave his countenance, against his name,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To laugh at gibing boys, and stand the push

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of every beardless vain comparative;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Grew a companion to the common streets,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Enfeoff’d himself to popularity,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That, being daily swallow’d by men’s eyes,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: They surfeited with honey, and began

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To loathe the taste of sweetness, whereof a little

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: More than a little is by much too much.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: So, when he had occasion to be seen,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: He was but as the cuckoo is in June,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Heard, not regarded; seen, but with such eyes

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: As, sick and blunted with community,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Afford no extraordinary gaze,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Such as is bent on sun-like majesty

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: When it shines seldom in admiring eyes,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But rather drowsed and hung their eyelids down,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Slept in his face, and render’d such aspect

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: As cloudy men use to their adversaries,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Being with his presence glutted, gorged, and full.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And in that very line, Harry, standest thou,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For thou hast lost thy princely privilege

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: With vile participation. Not an eye

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But is a-weary of thy common sight,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Save mine, which hath desired to see thee more,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Which now doth that I would not have it do,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Make blind itself with foolish tenderness.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I shall hereafter, my thrice gracious lord,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Be more myself.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For all the world

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: As thou art to this hour was Richard then

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: When I from France set foot at Ravenspurgh,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And even as I was then is Percy now.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Now, by my sceptre, and my soul to boot,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: He hath more worthy interest to the state

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Than thou, the shadow of succession.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For of no right, nor colour like to right,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: He doth fill fields with harness in the realm,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Turns head against the lion’s armed jaws,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And, being no more in debt to years than thou,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Leads ancient lords and reverend bishops on

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To bloody battles and to bruising arms.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: What never-dying honour hath he got

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Against renowned Douglas! whose high deeds,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Whose hot incursions and great name in arms,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Holds from all soldiers chief majority

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And military title capital

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Through all the kingdoms that acknowledge Christ.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thrice hath this Hotspur, Mars in swathing clothes,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: This infant warrior, in his enterprises

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Discomfited great Douglas, ta’en him once,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Enlarged him, and made a friend of him,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To fill the mouth of deep defiance up,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And shake the peace and safety of our throne.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And what say you to this? Percy, Northumberland,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The Archbishop’s Grace of York, Douglas, Mortimer,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Capitulate against us and are up.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But wherefore do I tell these news to thee?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Why, Harry, do I tell thee of my foes,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Which art my nearest and dearest enemy?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thou that art like enough, through vassal fear,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Base inclination, and the start of spleen,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To fight against me under Percy’s pay,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To dog his heels, and curtsy at his frowns,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To show how much thou art degenerate.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Do not think so, you shall not find it so.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And God forgive them that so much have sway’d

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Your Majesty’s good thoughts away from me!

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I will redeem all this on Percy’s head,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And, in the closing of some glorious day,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Be bold to tell you that I am your son,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: When I will wear a garment all of blood,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And stain my favours in a bloody mask,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Which, wash’d away, shall scour my shame with it.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And that shall be the day, whene’er it lights,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: That this same child of honour and renown,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: This gallant Hotspur, this all-praised knight,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And your unthought-of Harry chance to meet.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: For every honour sitting on his helm,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Would they were multitudes, and on my head

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: My shames redoubled! For the time will come,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: That I shall make this northern youth exchange

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: His glorious deeds for my indignities.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Percy is but my factor, good my lord,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: To engross up glorious deeds on my behalf,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And I will call him to so strict account

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: That he shall render every glory up,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Yea, even the slightest worship of his time,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Or I will tear the reckoning from his heart.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: This in the name of God I promise here,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: The which if He be pleased I shall perform,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I do beseech your Majesty may salve

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: The long-grown wounds of my intemperance.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: If not, the end of life cancels all bands,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And I will die a hundred thousand deaths

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Ere break the smallest parcel of this vow.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: A hundred thousand rebels die in this.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thou shalt have charge and sovereign trust herein.
Enter Sir Walter Blunt.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: How now, good Blunt? Thy looks are full of speed.

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: So hath the business that I come to speak of.

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: Lord Mortimer of Scotland hath sent word

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: That Douglas and the English rebels met

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: The eleventh of this month at Shrewsbury.

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: A mighty and a fearful head they are,

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: If promises be kept on every hand,

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: As ever offer’d foul play in a state.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The Earl of Westmoreland set forth today,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: With him my son, Lord John of Lancaster,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For this advertisement is five days old.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: On Wednesday next you, Harry, shall set forward,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: On Thursday we ourselves will march.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Our meeting is Bridgenorth. And, Harry, you

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Shall march through Gloustershire; by which account,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Our business valued, some twelve days hence

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Our general forces at Bridgenorth shall meet.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Our hands are full of business. Let’s away,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Advantage feeds him fat while men delay.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Eastcheap. A Room in the Boar’s Head Tavern.

lines.text: Enter Falstaff and Bardolph.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Bardolph, am I not fallen away vilely since this last action? Do I not

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: bate? Do I not dwindle? Why, my skin hangs about me like an old lady’s

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: loose gown. I am withered like an old apple-john. Well, I’ll repent,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: and that suddenly, while I am in some liking. I shall be out of heart

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: shortly, and then I shall have no strength to repent. An I have not

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: forgotten what the inside of a church is made of, I am a peppercorn, a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: brewer’s horse. The inside of a church! Company, villainous company,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: hath been the spoil of me.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Sir John, you are so fretful, you cannot live long.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Why, there is it. Come, sing me a song, make me merry. I was as

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: virtuously given as a gentleman need to be, virtuous enough; swore

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: little; diced not above seven times—a week; went to a bawdy house not

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: above once in a quarter—in an hour; paid money that I borrowed—three or

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: four times; lived well and in good compass; and now I live out of all

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: order, out of all compass.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Why, you are so fat, Sir John, that you must needs be out of all

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: compass, out of all reasonable compass, Sir John.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Do thou amend thy face, and I’ll amend my life. Thou art our admiral,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: thou bearest the lantern in the poop, but ’tis in the nose of thee.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Thou art the Knight of the Burning Lamp.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Why, Sir John, my face does you no harm.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: No, I’ll be sworn, I make as good use of it as many a man doth of a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: death’s-head or a _memento mori_. I never see thy face but I think upon

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: hell-fire, and Dives that lived in purple, for there he is in his

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: robes, burning, burning. If thou wert any way given to virtue, I would

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: swear by thy face. My oath should be, “By this fire, that’s God’s

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: angel.” But thou art altogether given over; and wert indeed, but for

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the light in thy face, the son of utter darkness. When thou ran’st up

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Gad’s Hill in the night to catch my horse, if I did not think thou

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: hadst been an _ignis fatuus_ or a ball of wildfire, there’s no purchase

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: in money. O, thou art a perpetual triumph, an everlasting

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: bonfire-light! Thou hast saved me a thousand marks in links and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: torches, walking with thee in the night betwixt tavern and tavern: but

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the sack that thou hast drunk me would have bought me lights as good

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: cheap at the dearest chandler’s in Europe. I have maintained that

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: salamander of yours with fire any time this two-and-thirty years, God

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: reward me for it!

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: ’Sblood, I would my face were in your belly!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: God-a-mercy! so should I be sure to be heartburnt.
Enter the Hostess.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: How now, Dame Partlet the hen, have you enquired yet who picked my

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: pocket?

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Why, Sir John, what do you think, Sir John, do you think I keep thieves

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: in my house? I have searched, I have enquired, so has my husband, man

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: by man, boy by boy, servant by servant. The tithe of a hair was never

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: lost in my house before.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Ye lie, hostess. Bardolph was shaved and lost many a hair, and I’ll be

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: sworn my pocket was picked. Go to, you are a woman, go.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Who, I? No; I defy thee: God’s light, I was never called so in mine own

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: house before.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Go to, I know you well enough.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: No, Sir John, you do not know me, Sir John. I know you, Sir John, you

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: owe me money, Sir John, and now you pick a quarrel to beguile me of it.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: I bought you a dozen of shirts to your back.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Dowlas, filthy dowlas. I have given them away to bakers’ wives; and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: they have made bolters of them.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Now, as I am a true woman, holland of eight shillings an ell. You owe

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: money here besides, Sir John, for your diet and by-drinkings, and money

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: lent you, four-and-twenty pound.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: He had his part of it, let him pay.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: He? Alas, he is poor, he hath nothing.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: How? Poor? Look upon his face. What call you rich? Let them coin his

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: nose, let them coin his cheeks. I’ll not pay a denier. What, will you

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: make a younker of me? Shall I not take mine ease in mine inn but I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: shall have my pocket picked? I have lost a seal-ring of my

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: grandfather’s worth forty mark.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: O Jesu, I have heard the Prince tell him, I know not how oft, that that

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: ring was copper.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: How? The Prince is a Jack, a sneak-up. ’Sblood, an he were here, I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: would cudgel him like a dog if he would say so.
Enter Prince Henry with Peto, marching. Falstaff meets him, playing on his truncheon like a fife.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: How now, lad? Is the wind in that door, i’faith? Must we all march?

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Yea, two and two, Newgate fashion.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: My lord, I pray you, hear me.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What say’st thou, Mistress Quickly? How doth thy husband? I love him

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: well; he is an honest man.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Good my lord, hear me.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Prithee, let her alone, and list to me.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What say’st thou, Jack?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: The other night I fell asleep here, behind the arras, and had my pocket

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: picked. This house is turned bawdy-house; they pick pockets.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What didst thou lose, Jack?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Wilt thou believe me, Hal, three or four bonds of forty pound apiece

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: and a seal-ring of my grandfather’s.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: A trifle, some eightpenny matter.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: So I told him, my lord, and I said I heard your Grace say so. And, my

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: lord, he speaks most vilely of you, like a foul-mouthed man as he is,

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: and said he would cudgel you.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What! he did not?

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: There’s neither faith, truth, nor womanhood in me else.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: There’s no more faith in thee than in a stewed prune, nor no more truth

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: in thee than in a drawn fox; and, for woman-hood, Maid Marian may be

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the deputy’s wife of the ward to thee. Go, you thing, go.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Say, what thing, what thing?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What thing? Why, a thing to thank God on.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: I am no thing to thank God on, I would thou shouldst know it! I am an

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: honest man’s wife, and, setting thy knighthood aside, thou art a knave

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: to call me so.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Setting thy womanhood aside, thou art a beast to say otherwise.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Say, what beast, thou knave, thou?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What beast? Why, an otter.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: An otter, Sir John? Why an otter?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Why, she’s neither fish nor flesh; a man knows not where to have her.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Thou art an unjust man in saying so, thou or any man knows where to

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: have me, thou knave, thou.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Thou say’st true, hostess, and he slanders thee most grossly.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: So he doth you, my lord, and said this other day you ought him a

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: thousand pound.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Sirrah, do I owe you a thousand pound?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: A thousand pound, Hal? A million. Thy love is worth a million; thou

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: owest me thy love.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Nay, my lord, he call’d you Jack, and said he would cudgel you.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Did I, Bardolph?

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Indeed, Sir John, you said so.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Yea, if he said my ring was copper.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I say ’tis copper. Darest thou be as good as thy word now?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Why, Hal, thou knowest, as thou art but man, I dare, but as thou art

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: prince, I fear thee as I fear the roaring of the lion’s whelp.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And why not as the lion?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: The King himself is to be feared as the lion. Dost thou think I’ll fear

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: thee as I fear thy father? Nay, an I do, I pray God my girdle break.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: O, if it should, how would thy guts fall about thy knees! But, sirrah,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: there’s no room for faith, truth, nor honesty in this bosom of thine;

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: it is all filled up with midriff. Charge an honest woman with picking

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: thy pocket! Why, thou whoreson, impudent, embossed rascal, if there

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: were anything in thy pocket but tavern reckonings, memorandums of bawdy

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: houses, and one poor pennyworth of sugar-candy to make thee

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: long-winded, if thy pocket were enriched with any other injuries but

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: these, I am a villain. And yet you will stand to it, you will not

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: pocket up wrong. Art thou not ashamed!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Dost thou hear, Hal? Thou knowest in the state of innocency Adam fell,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: and what should poor Jack Falstaff do in the days of villainy? Thou

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: seest I have more flesh than another man and therefore more frailty.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: You confess, then, you picked my pocket?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: It appears so by the story.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Hostess, I forgive thee. Go make ready breakfast, love thy husband,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: look to thy servants, cherish thy guests. Thou shalt find me tractable

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: to any honest reason. Thou seest I am pacified still. Nay, prithee, be

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: gone.
[_Exit Hostess._]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Now, Hal, to the news at court. For the robbery, lad, how is that

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: answered?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: O, my sweet beef, I must still be good angel to thee. The money is paid

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: back again.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: O, I do not like that paying back, ’tis a double labour.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I am good friends with my father, and may do anything.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Rob me the exchequer the first thing thou dost, and do it with unwashed

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: hands too.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Do, my lord.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I have procured thee, Jack, a charge of foot.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I would it had been of horse. Where shall I find one that can steal

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: well? O, for a fine thief, of the age of two-and-twenty or thereabouts!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I am heinously unprovided. Well, God be thanked for these rebels; they

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: offend none but the virtuous. I laud them, I praise them.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Bardolph!

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: My lord?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Go bear this letter to Lord John of Lancaster,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: To my brother John; this to my Lord of Westmoreland.
[_Exit Bardolph._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Go, Peto, to horse, to horse, for thou and I

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Have thirty miles to ride yet ere dinner-time.
[_Exit Peto._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Jack, meet me tomorrow in the Temple hall

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: At two o’clock in the afternoon;

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: There shalt thou know thy charge, and there receive

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Money and order for their furniture.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: The land is burning, Percy stands on high,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And either we or they must lower lie.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Rare words! Brave world!—Hostess, my breakfast, come.—

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: O, I could wish this tavern were my drum.
[_Exit._]
Enter Hotspur, Worcester and Douglas.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Well said, my noble Scot. If speaking truth

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: In this fine age were not thought flattery,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Such attribution should the Douglas have

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: As not a soldier of this season’s stamp

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Should go so general current through the world.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: By God, I cannot flatter, I do defy

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: The tongues of soothers, but a braver place

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: In my heart’s love hath no man than yourself.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Nay, task me to my word; approve me, lord.

lines.speaker: DOUGLAS
lines.text: Thou art the king of honour.

lines.speaker: DOUGLAS
lines.text: No man so potent breathes upon the ground

lines.speaker: DOUGLAS
lines.text: But I will beard him.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Do so, and ’tis well.
Enter a Messenger with letters.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: What letters hast thou there? I can but thank you.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: These letters come from your father.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Letters from him! Why comes he not himself?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: He cannot come, my lord, he is grievous sick.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Zounds, how has he the leisure to be sick

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: In such a justling time? Who leads his power?

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Under whose government come they along?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: His letters bear his mind, not I, my lord.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: I prithee, tell me, doth he keep his bed?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: He did, my lord, four days ere I set forth,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And at the time of my departure thence

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: He was much fear’d by his physicians.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: I would the state of time had first been whole

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Ere he by sickness had been visited.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: His health was never better worth than now.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Sick now? Droop now? This sickness doth infect

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: The very life-blood of our enterprise;

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: ’Tis catching hither, even to our camp.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: He writes me here, that inward sickness—

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And that his friends by deputation could not

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: So soon be drawn, nor did he think it meet

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: To lay so dangerous and dear a trust

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: On any soul removed but on his own.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Yet doth he give us bold advertisement

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: That with our small conjunction we should on,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: To see how fortune is disposed to us;

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: For, as he writes, there is no quailing now,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Because the King is certainly possess’d

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Of all our purposes. What say you to it?

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Your father’s sickness is a maim to us.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: A perilous gash, a very limb lopp’d off—

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And yet, in faith, it is not! His present want

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Seems more than we shall find it. Were it good

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: To set the exact wealth of all our states

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: All at one cast? To set so rich a main

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: On the nice hazard of one doubtful hour?

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: It were not good, for therein should we read

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: The very bottom and the soul of hope,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: The very list, the very utmost bound

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Of all our fortunes.

lines.speaker: DOUGLAS
lines.text: Faith, and so we should, where now remains

lines.speaker: DOUGLAS
lines.text: A sweet reversion. We may boldly spend

lines.speaker: DOUGLAS
lines.text: Upon the hope of what is to come in.

lines.speaker: DOUGLAS
lines.text: A comfort of retirement lives in this.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: A rendezvous, a home to fly unto,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: If that the devil and mischance look big

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Upon the maidenhead of our affairs.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: But yet I would your father had been here.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: The quality and hair of our attempt

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Brooks no division. It will be thought

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: By some that know not why he is away,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: That wisdom, loyalty, and mere dislike

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Of our proceedings, kept the Earl from hence.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: And think how such an apprehension

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: May turn the tide of fearful faction,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: And breed a kind of question in our cause.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: For well you know we of the off’ring side

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Must keep aloof from strict arbitrement,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: And stop all sight-holes, every loop from whence

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: The eye of reason may pry in upon us.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: This absence of your father’s draws a curtain

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: That shows the ignorant a kind of fear

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Before not dreamt of.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: You strain too far.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: I rather of his absence make this use:

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: It lends a lustre and more great opinion,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: A larger dare to our great enterprise,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Than if the Earl were here; for men must think

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: If we without his help can make a head

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: To push against the kingdom, with his help

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: We shall o’erturn it topsy-turvy down.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Yet all goes well, yet all our joints are whole.

lines.speaker: DOUGLAS
lines.text: As heart can think. There is not such a word

lines.speaker: DOUGLAS
lines.text: Spoke in Scotland as this term of fear.
Enter Sir Richard Vernon.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: My cousin Vernon! Welcome, by my soul.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Pray God my news be worth a welcome, lord.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: The Earl of Westmoreland, seven thousand strong,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Is marching hitherwards, with him Prince John.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: No harm, what more?

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: And further, I have learn’d

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: The King himself in person is set forth,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Or hitherwards intended speedily,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: With strong and mighty preparation.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: He shall be welcome too. Where is his son,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: The nimble-footed madcap Prince of Wales,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And his comrades, that daffed the world aside

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And bid it pass?

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: All furnish’d, all in arms;

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: All plumed like estridges that with the wind

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Bated like eagles having lately bathed,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Glittering in golden coats, like images,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: As full of spirit as the month of May,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: And gorgeous as the sun at midsummer;

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Wanton as youthful goats, wild as young bulls.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: I saw young Harry with his beaver on,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: His cuisses on his thighs, gallantly arm’d,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Rise from the ground like feather’d Mercury,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: And vaulted with such ease into his seat

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: As if an angel dropp’d down from the clouds,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: To turn and wind a fiery Pegasus,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: And witch the world with noble horsemanship.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: No more, no more! Worse than the sun in March,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: This praise doth nourish agues. Let them come!

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: They come like sacrifices in their trim,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And to the fire-eyed maid of smoky war

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: All hot and bleeding will we offer them.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: The mailed Mars shall on his altar sit

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Up to the ears in blood. I am on fire

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: To hear this rich reprisal is so nigh,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And yet not ours. Come, let me taste my horse,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Who is to bear me like a thunderbolt

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Against the bosom of the Prince of Wales.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Harry to Harry shall, hot horse to horse,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Meet and ne’er part till one drop down a corse.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: O, that Glendower were come!

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: There is more news.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: I learn’d in Worcester, as I rode along,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: He cannot draw his power this fourteen days.

lines.speaker: DOUGLAS
lines.text: That’s the worst tidings that I hear of yet.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Ay, by my faith, that bears a frosty sound.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: What may the King’s whole battle reach unto?

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: To thirty thousand.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Forty let it be.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: My father and Glendower being both away,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: The powers of us may serve so great a day.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Come, let us take a muster speedily.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Doomsday is near; die all, die merrily.

lines.speaker: DOUGLAS
lines.text: Talk not of dying. I am out of fear

lines.speaker: DOUGLAS
lines.text: Of death or death’s hand for this one half year.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Falstaff and Bardolph.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Bardolph, get thee before to Coventry; fill me a bottle of sack. Our

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: soldiers shall march through; we’ll to Sutton Co’fil’ tonight.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Will you give me money, captain?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Lay out, lay out.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: This bottle makes an angel.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: An if it do, take it for thy labour. An if it make twenty, take them

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: all, I’ll answer the coinage. Bid my lieutenant Peto meet me at town’s

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: end.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: I will, captain: farewell.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: If I be not ashamed of my soldiers, I am a soused gurnet. I have

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: misused the King’s press damnably. I have got, in exchange of a hundred

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: and fifty soldiers, three hundred and odd pounds. I press me none but

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: good householders, yeomen’s sons, inquire me out contracted bachelors,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: such as had been asked twice on the banns, such a commodity of warm

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: slaves as had as lief hear the devil as a drum, such as fear the report

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: of a caliver worse than a struck fowl or a hurt wild duck. I pressed me

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: none but such toasts-and-butter, with hearts in their bellies no bigger

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: than pins’ heads, and they have bought out their services; and now my

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: whole charge consists of ancients, corporals, lieutenants, gentlemen of

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: companies—slaves as ragged as Lazarus in the painted cloth, where the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: glutton’s dogs licked his sores; and such as indeed were never

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: soldiers, but discarded unjust servingmen, younger sons to younger

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: brothers, revolted tapsters, and ostlers trade-fallen; the cankers of a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: calm world and a long peace, ten times more dishonourable-ragged than

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: an old fazed ancient; and such have I to fill up the rooms of them that

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: have bought out their services, that you would think that I had a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: hundred and fifty tattered prodigals lately come from swine-keeping,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: from eating draff and husks. A mad fellow met me on the way, and told

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: me I had unloaded all the gibbets and pressed the dead bodies. No eye

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: hath seen such scarecrows. I’ll not march through Coventry with them,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: that’s flat. Nay, and the villains march wide betwixt the legs as if

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: they had gyves on, for indeed I had the most of them out of prison.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: There’s not a shirt and a half in all my company, and the half shirt is

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: two napkins tacked together and thrown over the shoulders like a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: herald’s coat without sleeves; and the shirt, to say the truth, stolen

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: from my host at Saint Albans, or the red-nose innkeeper of Daventry.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: But that’s all one; they’ll find linen enough on every hedge.
Enter Prince Henry and the Lord of Westmoreland.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: How now, blown Jack? How now, quilt?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What, Hal! How now, mad wag? What a devil dost thou in Warwickshire? My

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: good Lord of Westmoreland, I cry you mercy. I thought your honour had

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: already been at Shrewsbury.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Faith, Sir John, ’tis more than time that I were there, and you too,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: but my powers are there already. The King, I can tell you, looks for us

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: all. We must away all night.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Tut, never fear me. I am as vigilant as a cat to steal cream.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I think, to steal cream indeed, for thy theft hath already made thee

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: butter. But tell me, Jack, whose fellows are these that come after?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Mine, Hal, mine.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I did never see such pitiful rascals.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Tut, tut, good enough to toss; food for powder, food for powder,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: they’ll fill a pit as well as better. Tush, man, mortal men, mortal

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: men.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Ay, but, Sir John, methinks they are exceeding poor and bare, too

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: beggarly.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Faith, for their poverty, I know not where they had that; and for their

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: bareness, I am sure they never learned that of me.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: No, I’ll be sworn, unless you call three fingers on the ribs bare. But,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: sirrah, make haste. Percy is already in the field.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What, is the King encamped?

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: He is, Sir John. I fear we shall stay too long.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Well,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: To the latter end of a fray and the beginning of a feast

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Fits a dull fighter and a keen guest.
[_Exit._]
Enter Hotspur, Worcester, Douglas and Vernon.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: We’ll fight with him tonight.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: It may not be.

lines.speaker: DOUGLAS
lines.text: You give him then advantage.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Not a whit.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Why say you so? Looks he not for supply?

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: So do we.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: His is certain, ours is doubtful.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Good cousin, be advised, stir not tonight.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Do not, my lord.

lines.speaker: DOUGLAS
lines.text: You do not counsel well.

lines.speaker: DOUGLAS
lines.text: You speak it out of fear and cold heart.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Do me no slander, Douglas; by my life,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: And I dare well maintain it with my life,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: If well-respected honour bid me on,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: I hold as little counsel with weak fear

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: As you, my lord, or any Scot that this day lives.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Let it be seen tomorrow in the battle

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Which of us fears.

lines.speaker: DOUGLAS
lines.text: Yea, or tonight.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Content.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Tonight, say I.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Come, come, it may not be. I wonder much,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Being men of such great leading as you are,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: That you foresee not what impediments

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Drag back our expedition. Certain horse

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Of my cousin Vernon’s are not yet come up.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Your uncle Worcester’s horse came but today,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: And now their pride and mettle is asleep,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Their courage with hard labour tame and dull,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: That not a horse is half the half himself.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: So are the horses of the enemy

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: In general, journey-bated and brought low.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: The better part of ours are full of rest.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: The number of the King exceedeth ours.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: For God’s sake, cousin, stay till all come in.
[_The trumpet sounds a parley._]
Enter Sir Walter Blunt.

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: I come with gracious offers from the King,

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: If you vouchsafe me hearing and respect.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Welcome, Sir Walter Blunt, and would to God

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: You were of our determination!

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Some of us love you well, and even those some

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Envy your great deservings and good name,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Because you are not of our quality,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: But stand against us like an enemy.

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: And God defend but still I should stand so,

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: So long as out of limit and true rule

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: You stand against anointed majesty.

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: But to my charge. The King hath sent to know

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: The nature of your griefs, and whereupon

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: You conjure from the breast of civil peace

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: Such bold hostility, teaching his duteous land

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: Audacious cruelty. If that the King

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: Have any way your good deserts forgot,

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: Which he confesseth to be manifold,

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: He bids you name your griefs, and with all speed

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: You shall have your desires with interest

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: And pardon absolute for yourself and these

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: Herein misled by your suggestion.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: The King is kind, and well we know the King

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Knows at what time to promise, when to pay.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: My father and my uncle and myself

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Did give him that same royalty he wears,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And when he was not six-and-twenty strong,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Sick in the world’s regard, wretched and low,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: A poor unminded outlaw sneaking home,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: My father gave him welcome to the shore:

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And when he heard him swear and vow to God

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: He came but to be Duke of Lancaster,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: To sue his livery, and beg his peace

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: With tears of innocence and terms of zeal,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: My father, in kind heart and pity moved,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Swore him assistance, and performed it too.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Now, when the lords and barons of the realm

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Perceived Northumberland did lean to him,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: The more and less came in with cap and knee,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Met him in boroughs, cities, villages,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Attended him on bridges, stood in lanes,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Laid gifts before him, proffer’d him their oaths,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Give him their heirs as pages, follow’d him

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Even at the heels in golden multitudes.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: He presently, as greatness knows itself,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Steps me a little higher than his vow

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Made to my father while his blood was poor

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Upon the naked shore at Ravenspurgh;

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And now forsooth takes on him to reform

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Some certain edicts and some strait decrees

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: That lie too heavy on the commonwealth;

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Cries out upon abuses, seems to weep

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Over his country’s wrongs; and by this face,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: This seeming brow of justice, did he win

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: The hearts of all that he did angle for;

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Proceeded further—cut me off the heads

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Of all the favourites that the absent King

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: In deputation left behind him here

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: When he was personal in the Irish war.

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: Tut, I came not to hear this.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Then to the point.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: In short time after, he deposed the King,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Soon after that deprived him of his life,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And, in the neck of that, task’d the whole state.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: To make that worse, suffer’d his kinsman March

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: (Who is, if every owner were well placed,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Indeed his king) to be engaged in Wales,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: There without ransom to lie forfeited;

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Disgraced me in my happy victories,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Sought to entrap me by intelligence,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Rated mine uncle from the Council-board,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: In rage dismiss’d my father from the court,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Broke oath on oath, committed wrong on wrong,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And in conclusion drove us to seek out

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: This head of safety, and withal to pry

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Into his title, the which now we find

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Too indirect for long continuance.

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: Shall I return this answer to the King?

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Not so, Sir Walter. We’ll withdraw awhile.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Go to the King, and let there be impawn’d

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Some surety for a safe return again,

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And in the morning early shall my uncle

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: Bring him our purposes. And so, farewell.

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: I would you would accept of grace and love.

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: And maybe so we shall.

lines.speaker: BLUNT
lines.text: Pray God you do.

lines.text: This is not well, my lord, this is not well.

lines.text: Hear me, my liege:

lines.text: For mine own part, I could be well content

lines.text: You have not sought it? How comes it, then?

lines.text: Of favour from myself and all our house;

lines.text: And yet I must remember you, my lord,

lines.text: We were the first and dearest of your friends.

lines.text: For you my staff of office did I break

lines.text: In Richard’s time, and posted day and night

lines.text: To meet you on the way, and kiss your hand,

lines.text: When yet you were in place and in account

lines.text: Nothing so strong and fortunate as I.

lines.text: It was myself, my brother, and his son,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: That brought you home, and boldly did outdare

lines.text: The dangers of the time. You swore to us,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: And you did swear that oath at Doncaster,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: That you did nothing purpose ’gainst the state,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Nor claim no further than your new-fall’n right,

lines.text: The seat of Gaunt, dukedom of Lancaster.

lines.text: To this we swore our aid. But in short space

lines.text: It rain’d down fortune show’ring on your head,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: And such a flood of greatness fell on you,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: What with our help, what with the absent King,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: What with the injuries of a wanton time,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: The seeming sufferances that you had borne,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: And the contrarious winds that held the King

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: So long in his unlucky Irish wars

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: That all in England did repute him dead:

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: And from this swarm of fair advantages

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: You took occasion to be quickly woo’d

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: To gripe the general sway into your hand,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Forgot your oath to us at Doncaster;

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: And, being fed by us, you used us so

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: As that ungentle gull, the cuckoo’s bird,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Useth the sparrow—did oppress our nest,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Grew by our feeding to so great a bulk

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: That even our love durst not come near your sight

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: For fear of swallowing; but with nimble wing

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: We were enforced, for safety sake to fly

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Out of your sight, and raise this present head,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Whereby we stand opposed by such means

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: As you yourself have forged against yourself,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: By unkind usage, dangerous countenance,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: And violation of all faith and troth

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Sworn to us in your younger enterprise.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: These things, indeed, you have articulate,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Proclaim’d at market crosses, read in churches,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To face the garment of rebellion

lines.text: With some fine colour that may please the eye

lines.speaker: KING

lines.speaker: KING

lines.speaker: KING

lines.speaker: KING

lines.text: In both your armies there is many a soul

lines.speaker: PRINCE

lines.text: This present enterprise set off his head,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I do not think a braver gentleman,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: More active-valiant or more valiant-young,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: More daring or more bold, is now alive

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: To grace this latter age with noble deeds.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: For my part, I may speak it to my shame,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I have a truant been to chivalry,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And so I hear he doth account me too.

lines.text: Yet this before my father’s Majesty—

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I am content that he shall take the odds

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Of his great name and estimation,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And will, to save the blood on either side,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Try fortune with him in a single fight.

lines.text: And, Prince of Wales, so dare we venture thee,

lines.speaker: KING

lines.speaker: KING

lines.text: Rebuke and dread correction wait on us,

lines.speaker: KING

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: We will not now be troubled with reply.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: We offer fair, take it advisedly.

lines.text: It will not be accepted, on my life.

lines.text: The Douglas and the Hotspur both together

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Are confident against the world in arms.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Hence, therefore, every leader to his charge;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For on their answer, will we set on them,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And God befriend us as our cause is just!

lines.text: point of friendship.

lines.text: Say thy prayers, and farewell.

lines.text: I would ’twere bedtime, Hal, and all well.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Why, thou owest God a death.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: ’Tis not due yet, I would be loth to pay Him before His day. What need

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I be so forward with Him that calls not on me? Well, ’tis no matter,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: honour pricks me on. Yea, but how if honour prick me off when I come

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: on? How then? Can honor set to a leg? No. Or an arm? No. Or take away

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the grief of a wound? No. Honour hath no skill in surgery then? No.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What is honour? A word. What is in that word, “honour”? What is that

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: “honour”? Air. A trim reckoning! Who hath it? He that died o’

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Wednesday. Doth he feel it? No. Doth be hear it? No. ’Tis insensible,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: then? Yea, to the dead. But will it not live with the living? No. Why?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Detraction will not suffer it. Therefore I’ll none of it. Honour is a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: mere scutcheon. And so ends my catechism.
[_Exit._]
Enter Worcester and Vernon.

lines.text: O no, my nephew must not know, Sir Richard,

lines.text: The liberal and kind offer of the King.

lines.text: Then are we all undone.

lines.text: It is not possible, it cannot be,

lines.text: The King should keep his word in loving us;

lines.text: He will suspect us still, and find a time

lines.text: To punish this offence in other faults.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Suspicion all our lives shall be stuck full of eyes,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: For treason is but trusted like the fox,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Who, ne’er so tame, so cherish’d and lock’d up,

lines.text: Will have a wild trick of his ancestors.

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: Look how we can, or sad or merrily,

lines.text: Interpretation will misquote our looks,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: And we shall feed like oxen at a stall,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: The better cherish’d still the nearer death.

lines.text: My nephew’s trespass may be well forgot,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: It hath the excuse of youth and heat of blood,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: And an adopted name of privilege—

lines.text: A hare-brain’d Hotspur, govern’d by a spleen.

lines.text: All his offences live upon my head

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: And on his father’s. We did train him on,

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: And, his corruption being ta’en from us,

lines.text: We as the spring of all shall pay for all.

lines.text: Therefore, good cousin, let not Harry know

lines.speaker: WORCESTER
lines.text: In any case the offer of the King.

lines.text: Arm, gentlemen; to arms! For I have thrown

lines.text: Did hear a challenge urged more modestly,

lines.text: Unless a brother should a brother dare

lines.text: Trimm’d up your praises with a princely tongue,

lines.text: Spoke your deservings like a chronicle,

lines.text: By still dispraising praise valued with you,

lines.text: And, which became him like a prince indeed,

lines.text: He made a blushing cital of himself,

lines.text: And chid his truant youth with such a grace

lines.text: As if he master’d there a double spirit

lines.text: Of teaching and of learning instantly.

lines.text: There did he pause: but let me tell the world,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: If he outlive the envy of this day,

lines.text: Cousin, I think thou art enamoured

lines.text: Upon his follies. Never did I hear

lines.text: Of any prince so wild a liberty.

lines.text: But be he as he will, yet once ere night

lines.text: I will embrace him with a soldier’s arm,

lines.text: That he shall shrink under my courtesy.

lines.text: Arm, arm with speed! And, fellows, soldiers, friends,

lines.text: My lord, here are letters for you.

lines.text: I cannot read them now.—

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: O gentlemen, the time of life is short!

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: To spend that shortness basely were too long

lines.speaker: HOTSPUR
lines.text: If life did ride upon a dial’s point,
